analysis.title: North America Hardware & Storage C3Q26 Previews: Broad Enterprise Demand & AI Buildouts Outweigh PC Softness; Prefer DELL, HPE, P
key_insights: Citi expects strong enterprise infrastructure OEM results, citing a broader refresh cycle backed by its 3Q CIO survey, VAR checks, and constructive comments from OEMs and suppliers (Cisco, Arista, CDW).

AI infrastructure demand appears robust per commentary from SMCI, CoreWeave, TSMC, Taiwan supply chain and Wistron. Peak-AI-demand and 'over-earning' fears (pull-forward demand, memory prices stabilizing) have compressed multiples and share prices during the quarter.
PCs weakened on negative IDC datapoints and Intel earnings. Citi prefers DELL, HPE and Everpure (P) and keeps Neutral on NTAP and HPQ.

DELL (reports Nov 24): Buy kept, target cut to $550 from $600 on a 16x P/E (was 18x) due to multiple compression across traditional hardware peers. Shares are down more than 30% and valuation relative to Citi's growth estimates is near COVID-era trough levels.

DELL OctQ estimates: revenue $49.7B (+84% y/y), EPS $6.75 (+161% y/y) vs Street $49.2B / $6.56 and guidance $49B +/- $0.5B / $6.50 +/- $0.10. JanQ: revenue $53.7B (+61% y/y), EPS $7.51 vs Street $53.5B / $7.45.

DELL: AI servers carry lower gross margin and are a partial margin headwind. Citi sees possible storage upside in 2H, remains cautious on the CSG (PC) segment, and cites an AI deal pipeline of multiples of its $95B backlog. Enterprise AI customers rose to 6,500 from 5,000 the prior quarter.

HPE (reports Nov 23): Buy kept, target cut to $80 from $92 on 14x P/E (was 16x). F4Q model: revenue $14.4B, EPS $1.28 vs consensus $14.35B / $1.27. Jan quarter: revenue $13.5B, EPS $1.08 vs consensus $12.8B / $1.05.

HPE drivers: last quarter's server orders grew 75% y/y, a $3.5B hyperscaler server win, AI server revenue modeled above $2B in F4Q, and Cloud & AI operating margin modeled at 15.4% vs 17%. Networking FY27 growth outlook raised to high-teens to low-20%, Juniper synergies raised to $800M by FY28 from $600M. Management targets a return to buybacks in F4Q.

NTAP (reports Dec 1): Neutral and $190 target kept. Citi expects OctQ revenue $2.2B (+27% y/y) and EPS $2.64 vs Street $2.1B / $2.60, at the high end of guidance. Valuation looks full given product margin pressure from NAND costs (TrendFocus expects NAND price increases of 10%-15% in 4Q) and limited share gains.

HPQ (reports Nov 24): Neutral and $25 target kept. Citi expects revenue $15.3B (+4% y/y) and EPS $0.74 (-20% y/y) vs Street $15.4B / $0.75. FY27 estimates are revenue $58.1B (-3%) and EPS $3.02 vs Street $60.9B / $3.19, below consensus. New CEO Emma Walmsley starts in January 2027. Tariff refunds add about $0.08 in Q4 after $0.11 in Q3.

Everpure (P) reports Nov 18 and carries a Positive Catalyst Watch under a Buy. Citi expects revenue of $1.33B (+38% y/y) and operating income of $275M, toward the high end of guidance. Hyperscaler penetration is about 2% of eSSD exabyte consumption, and the stock trades near 20x EV/EBIT.

Citi's 3Q VAR survey (N=54, up from 41) shows a cautious but improving hardware environment. AI servers are the strongest area, traditional servers are steady, storage is in line to slightly positive, and NTM spending views run 1-5 points above LTM.

Citi's CIO survey: IT budgets are expected to grow +3.4% over the next 12 months (US +3.9%, EMEA +1.8%). 41% of respondents revised budgets up, vs 28% last quarter. 54% see GenAI raising hardware budgets, vs 33% before.

Citi's AI team raised its global AI capex forecast to $1.68T in 2027E (+64% y/y) and $2.13T in 2028E (+27% y/y). AI infrastructure stocks are under pressure on deployment-risk worries: Nvidia roadmap and integration concerns, and neocloud financing risk.
The worldwide server market grew 52% y/y in Q2 2026 to $166.3B. Citi forecasts server spend of $835B in 2026 (+84%) and $1.26T in 2027 (+51%), with AI servers 71.4% of 2026 spend.

The external enterprise storage market grew 34% y/y to $10.3B in 2Q per IDC. Dell holds 24% share (+43% y/y), NetApp 10% (+36%) and Everpure 10% (+50%). Growth is driven more by pricing than capacity, and pull-forward ahead of component cost increases is part of the strength.

Networking demand is strong: Arista revenue grew 58.5% y/y in Q3 2026, and Cisco networking orders grew 28% y/y with campus refresh less than 10% penetrated. HPE sees the networking market growing at an 18% CAGR through 2029.

Worldwide PC shipments fell 20.1% y/y and 9.1% q/q to 62.7M in Q3 2026 on inventory pull-in ahead of memory-driven price hikes. Citi forecasts 4Q26E notebook shipments -9% q/q and -29% y/y, and 2H26 industry PC shipments -21% y/y, with -14% in 1H27.

Intel expects the 2026 PC unit TAM to fall about 12% (2H down more than 20%) and the 2027 TAM to fall about 10%, and does not expect memory conditions to improve in 2027. Some markets hold about 15 weeks of PC channel inventory, about double normal.
Print industry units fell 7.8% y/y and revenue fell 8.7% in 3Q, and IDC expects weak print demand through the rest of 2026.

market_movers.rationale: Target cut from $600 on a 16x P/E (was 18x) due to sector multiple compression. Citi cites durable AI and traditional server demand, improving storage, and a valuation near COVID-era troughs.
Target cut from $92 on 14x P/E (was 16x). Citi cites enterprise infrastructure strength, networking demand, improving storage, backlog conversion and a planned return to buybacks.
Enterprise storage checks are constructive, but valuation looks full given product margin pressure from NAND costs and limited share gains.
PC demand is weak with rising channel inventory and Citi's FY27 estimates sit below Street. Cost mitigation and premium mix partly offset component inflation.
Positive Catalyst Watch into Nov 18 earnings on enterprise storage demand, improving profitability and ramping hyperscaler opportunity.

sector_views.rationale: Refresh cycle, AI buildout and pricing are supporting demand, corroborated by CIO and VAR surveys.
Unit declines, channel inventory build, component cost inflation and lengthening replacement cycles weigh on demand.

earnings_insights: DELL OctQ (reports Nov 24), Citi estimate: revenue $49.7B (+84% y/y), EPS $6.75 (+161% y/y) vs Street estimate $49.2B / $6.56 and company guidance $49B +/- $0.5B / $6.50 +/- $0.10. JanQ Citi estimate: revenue $53.7B, EPS $7.51 vs Street estimate $53.5B / $7.45.
HPE F4Q (reports Nov 23), Citi estimate: revenue $14.4B, EPS $1.28 vs consensus $14.35B / $1.27. Jan quarter Citi estimate: revenue $13.5B, EPS $1.08 vs consensus $12.8B / $1.05.

NTAP OctQ (reports Dec 1), Citi estimate: revenue $2.2B (+27% y/y), EPS $2.64 (+29% y/y) vs Street estimate $2.1B / $2.60 and guidance $2.025B-$2.175B / $2.54-$2.64. FY27 Citi estimate: revenue $8.3B, EPS $10.01 vs Street $8.2B / $10.02.

HPQ OctQ (reports Nov 24), Citi estimate: revenue $15.3B (+4% y/y), EPS $0.74 (-20% y/y) vs Street estimate $15.4B / $0.75. FY27 Citi estimate: revenue $58.1B (-3%), EPS $3.02 (-7%) vs Street estimate $60.9B / $3.19.

Everpure OctQ (reports Nov 18), Citi estimate: revenue $1.33B (+38% y/y), operating income $275M (+40% y/y), toward the high end of guidance. FY27/FY28 revenue growth estimated at about 38%/42% with 19%/25% EBIT margins.
HPE management guided FY27 Cloud & AI growth of 14-18%, excluding the server component of the later Vultr deal, and raised its FY27 networking growth outlook to high-teens to low-20%.
HPQ expects tariff refunds of about $0.08 in Q4 after $0.11 in Q3, and management said Q4 should be the low point for Personal Systems margins.

macro_indicators.indicator: CIO survey IT budget growth, next twelve months
macro_indicators.interpretation: Budget expectations improved slightly from June and sit above historical averages, supporting enterprise hardware demand.
Inventory pull-in ahead of memory-driven price hikes and high prices broke the normal seasonal pattern.
AI infrastructure investment is driving growth, with unit growth of 15% and higher ASPs.
Second straight quarter of sharp acceleration, driven by delayed refreshes, AI demand and pricing.
Cloud capex estimates keep rising even as AI infrastructure stocks sell off on deployment risk.
Notebook ODMs are cutting shipment forecasts, with margin dilution expected across the notebook supply chain.
Intel does not expect memory conditions to improve in 2027, which constrains PC volumes.
Broad-based weakness across consumer and office print.

trade_ideas.description: Long Everpure (P) into Nov 18 earnings via a Positive Catalyst Watch
trade_ideas.rationale: Enterprise storage demand momentum, improving profitability and a ramping hyperscaler opportunity.

trade_ideas.description: Long DELL (Buy, $550 target) ahead of the Nov 24 print
trade_ideas.rationale: Durable AI and traditional server demand, improving storage and a valuation that already discounts substantial EPS compression.
trade_ideas.risk: Slower hardware recovery, PC refresh delays, an AI backlog that does not convert to revenue in CY2026.

trade_ideas.description: Long HPE (Buy, $80 target) ahead of the Nov 23 print
trade_ideas.rationale: Enterprise infrastructure and networking strength, backlog conversion and a return to buybacks in F4Q.
trade_ideas.risk: AI server mix eroding margins, share losses in server and storage, less AI demand than expected, FCF conversion.

risk_factors: Peak-AI-demand and over-earning concerns, including pull-forward demand and memory prices stabilizing.
Deployment risk and neocloud financing risk for AI infrastructure.
Component cost inflation (NAND, memory, CPU) pressuring product margins and demand, with persistent price increases testing IT budgets.
The debate over whether storage and hardware strength reflects pull-forward buying that could pause once pricing cools.
A mix shift to lower-margin AI servers.
PC channel inventory build, lengthening replacement cycles and share losses at Dell, Lenovo and HPQ.
Print weakness from energy costs and economic uncertainty.
vol_and_positioning: Citi describes DELL's valuation relative to its growth estimates as approaching COVID-era trough levels, with shares down more than 30%.
Share prices and multiples compressed during the quarter on peak-AI-demand and over-earning fears. The report includes a crowding scores exhibit but no figures in the text.
geopolitical: IDC attributes part of the print decline to the ongoing Middle East conflict and related energy-cost pressure.

tension_points.bull_case: Enterprise refresh, AI buildout and pricing are driving durable demand. Citi's VAR and CIO surveys point to NTM spending above LTM, and NetApp management cites structural AI-ready infrastructure demand.
tension_points.bear_case: Storage and hardware strength may reflect pull-forward buying ahead of price increases, with a possible spending pause if pricing cools and buyers wait for stability. Peak-AI-demand and over-earning fears have compressed multiples.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A spending pause once component pricing cools, or AI backlog that does not convert to revenue in CY2026.

tension_points.bull_case: Disciplined pricing, opex leverage (opex about 8% of revenue) and storage profitability offset AI server margin dilution.
tension_points.bear_case: A growing mix of lower-gross-margin AI servers remains a partial margin headwind, and neocloud customer exposure raises concern.
